question.text: A company has a fixed-rate bond and enters into an interest rate swap (pay floating, receive fixed) to hedge changes in its fair value. Under fair value hedge accounting, gains/losses on the swap are recognised in:

answer.text: Deferred in the balance sheet indefinitely

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook gives a fixed-rate bond hedged by an interest rate swap as the fair value hedge example. Under fair value hedge accounting, gains and losses on the hedging instrument (the swap) are recognised in the Statement of Profit and Loss. The hedged item (the fixed-rate bond) is also remeasured for changes in fair value attributable to the hedged risk through P&L. The Trap: A floating-rate loan hedged by a pay-fixed/receive-floating swap is a cash flow hedge fact pattern, where the effective portion of gains and losses goes to Other Comprehensive Income (equity), not P&L. The hedge type chosen determines which line item is hit. Note: The opposite leg of the rule is also workbook-backed: effective cash flow hedge gains or losses are recognised in equity (OCI). The fact pattern and the hedge type must match for the answer to apply cleanly.
